A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Newton min-max optimization work. All 30 pages of v4 and 32 pages of v5 support comparison of the text, equations, proofs, figures, and references. Neither contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original experiments on synthetic cubic-regularized bilinear problems and AUC maximization using three datasets.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original synthetic experiments and reports revised AUC comparisons, including variance-reduced and runtime results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain their update rules, inexactness conditions, Jacobian subsampling schemes, and Newton subproblem solver. Expanded explanations and changed experimental tolerances do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic problem with n = 50, 100, and 200, and the same AUC objective on a9a, covetype, and w8a. Removing Table 1 does not remove dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The AUC comparison adds SVREG from Alacaoglu and Malitsky (2022), while separate Algorithm 2 and SOGDA results disappear from Figure 2. v5 explains that SEG represents the similar stochastic EG/OGDA methods. The synthetic EG1, OGDA1, EG2, and OGDA2 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported subproblem tolerance kappa_m from 10^-8 to 10^-6. The revised AUC comparison specifies published defaults for SVREG and reports trajectories over roughly 20 epochs rather than 4–6. These disclosures do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v4's Algorithm 2 versus Algorithm 3 comparison supported the claim that subsampling reaches similar solution quality with fewer samples. v5 removes this comparison and its accompanying finding. The discussion of aggressive line-search parameters and instability is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The sampling failure-probability parameter is retained and is not newly introduced empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 2 substantially replaces the real-data results with revised convergence traces and new runtime outcomes. v5 shows SVREG improving on SEG but trailing Algorithm 3 across the three AUC datasets; v4 instead reports SEG, SOGDA, and two Newton variants using epoch plots only. Algorithm 2 and separate SOGDA result entries disappear. These are revised comparisons, not an established same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Definition 2.2 corrects the concavity inequality's gradient from gradient_x to gradient_y. The main convergence bounds and proofs remain substantively unchanged. However, revised Remark 4.8 newly calls phi(lambda) = sqrt(psi(lambda)) - lambda/(6 rho) concave, contradicting the retained convexity statement and reasoning in Proposition 4.5.

C1.justification: v5 withdraws the central claims of matching lower bounds and achieving order-optimal convergence from the title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion. It retains the O(epsilon^-2/3) upper bound and Schur-decomposition complexity, but reframes the contribution around practical inexact algorithms and explicitly acknowledges that the conceptual convergence proof is not new.

C2.justification: Revised Remark 4.2 explains why existing exact-oracle and fixed-error lower bounds do not establish optimality for the paper's decreasing-error Jacobian scheme. New Remark 4.14 identifies finite-sum minimax lower bounds as unresolved and discusses variance reduction or averaging as possible improvements. These materially qualify v4's interpretation of its guarantees.

D1.justification: The reported software changes from MATLAB R2023b to R2024b, and v5 documents the revised synthetic tolerance and SVREG parameter source. Hardware and the LIBSVM access information remain unchanged. Dataset sizes and dimensions move into Figure 2, but Table 1's reported [0,1] scaling information is lost.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands positioning around newer second-order methods, inexact-oracle lower bounds, and finite-sum variance reduction, including Chen, Agafonov, Alves, and Alacaoglu–Malitsky works. It more explicitly credits existing algorithmic components and acknowledges subsequent methods that match or surpass its guarantees. Kotsalis et al. (2022) is removed; publication updates to retained works are not new citations.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution narrative are substantially recast, including the research question, component attribution, and relationship to competing methods. Related-work passages and several explanatory remarks are extensively revised. The title and an affiliation change, while the overall six-section organization remains.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from three epoch panels to six epoch/runtime panels, with revised legends, axes, and dataset statistics in panel titles. Table 1 is removed. Algorithm boxes and equations reflow, but the general document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v5 improves scientific framing by withdrawing unsupported optimality claims and explaining the limits of available lower bounds. The SVREG comparison and actual runtime panels strengthen practical evaluation. These gains are tempered by losing the subsampling comparison and scaling disclosure, and by the new concave/convex contradiction in Remark 4.8. With the core methods and proofs largely unchanged, the net improvement is limited.
